verdict_text: NO. The script sets `DROP = {2, 6, 10, 15}`, dropping block 15 instead of block 14, which violates required-result clause 1 ("Remove every tensor of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14"). As a consequence the renumbering is also wrong: surviving blocks are `[0,1,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,12,13,14]`, so old 14 maps to new 11 whereas clause 2 requires old 15 → 11, and the values stored at new indices 8..11 come from old blocks 11,12,13,14 rather than 11,12,13,15. The output still has 184 tensors with contiguous indices 0..11, so both assertions pass and the failure is silent — exactly the "loads and runs, silently wrong" hazard the task describes — but grading against the hidden reference will fail on bit-exact values for the affected blocks. A minor secondary issue: the checks use bare `assert`, which is stripped under `python -O`, so the "fail loudly" guarantee is not unconditional.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
